I will keep all 13.1 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation. I have done this many years, and I do not start from zero every season. I look at what worked last year, what the neighbors around me are doing, and how much cash I can put into seed, fertilizer, water, and sprays. With well irrigation, I will not let the crop sit dry at the key time. I do not want to gamble on cutting fertilizer too hard, because losing yield hurts more than wasting a little fertilizer. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, keep fertilizer a bit on the safe side, water about three times, and spray for weeds and disease when needed. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed, sow right after wheat harvest, keep the stand full, push nitrogen a little harder than wheat, and give one or two waters depending on rain. On 13.1 mu, I still have to watch cost, so I will stay with rotary tillage for wheat land and no-tillage or direct seeding for maize after wheat, because that saves time and labor.
